cells.remarks: Traces the king's genealogy from Mûlarāja I and records his orders issued from Anahilapātaka, granting, on the occasion of a solar eclipse in Phālguna, two villages called Rajana- shara and Rājasamri to the feeding house created for the dēva and the matha of mother Salakhaṇadēvī, in Talapada of Maula(?). The grant was written by Kāyasthafalika Thakkura Sēmamha, son of Kāgastha Sātikara, and declared by sâdhika was Thakkura Vayajaidēva. A postscript declares: 'Vâchhaka was the Sthāvapati of sri-Mûlēśvaradēva-matha (cf. No. 13 above) and his successors as permanent trustees. Another postscript makes the possessors of the granted vil- lages responsible for robberies committed in them. Ibid., No. 534.

cells.remarks: Records the grant of 12 halas of land, 12 shops, etc., by Mahā-maṇḍalēśvara Rājaputra Sōmarāja, when stationed at Brāh-maṇḍa in the suva of Āśāpalli, to maintain a cistern and to provide daily food-offerings and services and to get the repair done in the temples of Ballālanārāyaṇa and Rūpa-nārāyaṇa, for the merit of the donor's grandfather Rāņaka Lūṇarāja and father Saṅgrāmasiṁha. The writer is Rāja-paṇḍita Śrīdhara, son of the minister Thakkura Sridhara of the minister Nāgada. The lulaka of the grant was Mahā-sāṁdhivigrahika Thakkura Sridhara and the writer was mahā-sāṁdhivigrahika sridharana. Ibid., No. 557.

cells.date: Śaka 915, Vijaya, (verse), Śrāvaṇa ba. 15, Sunday, solar eclipse = 993 A.D., August 20.
cells.remarks: Traces the genealogies of the Rāshṭrakūṭas from Gōvinda I to Kakkaļa and of the Śilāhāras from Kapardin to Aparājita. Records the king's orders issued from Sthāṇaka granting a garden in the village of Sālanaka to the Brāhmaṇa Kōlama-kramavīra who was the son of Haradēva and belonged to Kasyapa-gōtra and Sādala-śākhā. The donee's family is said to have hailed from Karahāṭa, to have been residing in Punaka-deśa and to have come to Sthāṇaka on business. Refers to the minister Kēmapārya and to Saudhī-vigrahin Jhaijhaiya. The writer of the grant was Kā-yastha Uddaṇa, son of Chakkaiya. Published by A. Ś. Gadha in Important Inscriptions from the Baroda State, Vol. I, pp. 55 ff.

cells.place: Slab from the Aṣtabhujasvāmin temple at Site No. 29.
cells.date: Year 30, Va. pāt 7, Prakrit, Brāhmī divasa 1.
cells.remarks: Records the installation, on the Sitāgiri, of the image of Lord Aṣtabhujasvāmin by several persons, viz., Mahāgrāmika Mahādaṇḍanāyaka Mahādaṇḍanāyaka Sivasepa belonging to Kauska-gōtra and the Pōribhēdha [clan], the Yavanarōdjas of Sañjayapura, Saṅghānilayā from Kuḍā, and Vadha, a citizen of the city of Sarakāra of Vanavāsa. Also records other pious acts apparently of the same persons such as decorating the enclosure [of the shrine of Aṣtabhujasvāmin] on the hill, cleansing of the well called Mahāmaṇḍa, excavation of two tanks, one on the Sitāgiri and the other at Karra, and planting a grove of mango trees. The engraver of the record was Vardhamānaka of the Siṃbaka family, Amātya Tiṣyabhārman is stated to have composed the record. In characters of the 3rd or 4th century A.D. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIV, pp. 197 ff.

cells.place: Broken pillar found near Site No. 9
cells.remarks: Damaged and fragmentary. Records the religious activities of an upāsikā named Chadāsiri (Chandrasrī), described as the daughter of many house-gifts and as the performer of religious ceremonies in honour of the teachers and the Satīgriha. The place where Chadāsiri performed the pious deeds recorded in the inscription is described as the Sethi-saṁnidi-maṇḍapa (Śreshṭhivāra-vardhamāna) in the Mahā-vihāra of Mahavana, built by Chantisiri at Vijayapuri on the Sriparvata. Also states that Chadāsiri set up a vihāra-khada (vihara-maṇḍapa) and a bhama-śālā (bhamān-śālā) for a particular Ariya-samgha (Ārya-samgha) with a view to attain-ing nirvāṇa. Do. Ibid., pp. 7-10. Cf. A.R.Ep., 1958-59, No. B 84 which is also published in Ep. Ind., op. cit., pp. 9-10.

cells.place: Panel of a lime-stone frieze depicting four principal events of the Buddha's life. From site No. 106 (Kumāranandi-vihāra).
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that the śaila-maṇḍapa pratimā of Bhagavat was installed at the Mahābodhi-pārśva at Vijayanapura on the Śeparvata by the śreshthin Kumāranandin who was a son of Īvamdatta and hailed from Syandakaparvata. He is stated to have performed the meritorious deed along with his wife, as well as for the welfare and increase of lives for the attainment of welfare and happiness for his own self and for all beings. Ibid., pp. 11-13.

cells.remarks: Records the construction of a well at Tarākpura or Tarāpura, (Dhana, dhana, Dhanya or Dhaniā) of the Tāmbali (Tām- biliya) varṇa for alleviating the distress due to drought. Dhanada was the son of Mumau of Bārakshatīya. His grandfather great-grandfather were Satrabhāṇa and Parshada. He belonged to the Mihāra family (i.e. Mêr community) devoted to the goddess Nāgavallī and is credited with the performance of many charitable and religious deeds. His grandfather Saihada also built many temples about our and at other localities on the step-well. The praśasti was composed by Hala who was a Nāgara-Brāhmaṇa. The step-well was constructed by Vanāka, son of sūtrādhāra Rājā and Khetāka, son of sūtrādhāra Dēvadāsa.

cells.remarks: Contains a praśasti recording the excavation of a step-well at Stambha-tīrtha by Mihra Dhanka (Dhana, Dhanā, Dhanya or Dhanads), son of Mihra Mukunda. Mêro (i.e. Mêr) is spelt in the vavified section as Mehīro and genealogically the descendants of Dhanada (Dhanā) are said. The excavation of the step-well was done by Va[n]āka, son of sūtrādhāra Rājā and Khetāka, son of sūtrādhāra Dēvadāsa, who are the same as Vanāka and Khêtāka in No. 209 above.

or Dhanads), son of Mihra Mukunda. Mêro (i.e. Mêr) is
spelt in the vavified section as Mehīro and genealogically
the descendants of Dhanada (Dhanā) are said. The ancestry
given in the record is the same as in No. 209 above, but
mentions Vijala under the name Vaijala and includes the
names of the wives of Mukarāds, Dhanā and Balarājia. The
excavation of the step-well was done by Va[n]āka, son of
sūtrādhāra Rājā and Khetāka, son of sūtrādhāra Dēvadāsa,
who are the same as Vanāka and Khêtāka in No. 209 above.Read more (1 KB)

cells.location: Vāmrā
cells.place: Two faces of a pillar in the Hanumān temple.
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama 47, Subhakrit, Pushya śu. 5, Sunday, Uttarā- yaṇa-saṅkrāmaṇa. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of 15 mādar of land for the god Rēvaṇēśvara by the queen Suggaladēvi at the request of Nāgarāja of the Vāji family, whose genealogy is described in the record. The temple is stated to have been constructed by Rēvaya, a local nobleman, who is also a grant of land by Nāga- rāja to the same temple. It is further stated that he made a grant of land belonging to Nāgarāhal for the Brāhmaṇas on the occasion of the installation of the deity, Śiva Svayaṁ- mbhu, by Rebba-dēvi, wife of Kalichōra. The same village is stated to have been granted for god Rēvaṇēśvara and for the Brāhmaṇas, by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Ereyamarasa.

cells.remarks: Records the erection of a memorial pillar styled balayashṭi which was a gūravashikā (i.e., family [pillar] of stone) by Varga-grāmika meant for the increase of yaśas and kīrti. Varga was the brother of Śrīdatta and Chhūṇḍaka and son of Sūrata and grandchild of Sūryadatta, grandson of Āvaḍara. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIII, pp. 306 ff.

cells.place:
SALEM DISTRICT
TIRUCHENGODU TALUK
Pālāmedu.—Stone in a field to the south Kings of Mysore
of the Īsvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records that the village of Pālāmeḍu was leased out to Gōpāla for 1000 varahas, which amount is required to be utilized for the repairs to the tank and temple, Lakshmī-Nārāyaṇa-sannidhi of the Āhōbala Sri-Parānkuśa-Rāmānuja-Jīyar matha and for the feeding of Śrīvaishnavas. The assignment is stated to have been made on the occasion of a lunar eclipse.

cells.date: Kali 4690, Kollam 844, Kiḷisaka, Kārtikai, śu. 13, Friday, Revati. The Kali and Kollam years do not agree.
cells.remarks: Indifferently engraved. Records that when the god at Tiru-kkurungudi was seated with his raniṣus on the maṇḍapa called Mahārāja's seat under the Uḍaiyār-nāmbi and Choḷakānta, there was present the mahājanāmbi and party who were the representative of Vadamalaiyappar and party who were the agents of Choḷakāṇgalayakkan assembled and accepted the land given for feeding Brāhmaṇas at the local choultry by Śrīkarakaran/drakamāku Śoḷagamāku Kaḷaiyappan.

cells.place:
SRIVAIKUNTAM TALUK
Cheyidunganallur.—Vyāghrapādīśvara temple, maḥāmaṇḍapa, north wall.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the land to the god Tiruppuli-īśvaram-uḍaiyār of Ātūr alias Tiruvarangaśaturvedimaṅgalam in Mura-p-pumāḍu as devadāna-iraiyili. The land is stated to have been enjoyed by Virasāladēvar after taking it over on mortgage from the sabhā of Kiḷimanalai. The charter is attested by twelve persons including the signatures of several officers of the puramavari-tinaikkalam including Kariyamālāgalan alias Uttamapāṇḍiya-vilupparaiyan of Kiḷinūr alias Kirtivislayanallur in Karuṅguḍi-nāḍu. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.location: Eksaṁbhi
cells.place: Slab set up inside the Ādinātha Basati
cells.date: Śaka 1087 (current), Phālguṇa śu. 13, Thursday = 1165 A.D., February 25.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land, house-site for a dānasālā, garden etc., for worship, offerings etc., to the Nimniṁdha basadi at Ekka-saṁbuge situated in Koravalī-gampanādu of Kuṇḍi pro-vince, by Kāctarivya of the Raṭṭa family. The basadi was got built by Kālaṇa, a subordinate of Appayyanāyaka, who was a subordinate of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kācaṇarasa. He made an endowment in favour of the basadi and entrusted it to mahā-maṇḍalāchārya Vijayakīrtti of Yāpaniyasangha and Puṇṇagavrikshamūlagana. The record contains genealogical accounts of Kālaṇa, Kāctarivya and Vijayakīrtti. It also registers an earlier gift of land by Appayyanāyaka to the same basadi by the five hundred svāmis of Ayyavōle, the 1700 gavares, mummuridandas, taḷa-samata and ubhaya-nānādēśis. Noticed in Mye. arch. Reports, 1916, pp. 48-50.

cells.remarks: Records the renewal of a gift of land in Muḍiyanahalli formerly granted by Perggade Nārāyaṇa, when Chuṇḍarāyasa was administering the country in the reign of Trailōkyamalla (Sōmēśvara I). The gift was renewed by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Udayāditya at the request of Sōmēśvara of Baḷḷigāve, for the worship of the deity Mūkamādēva and for the worship of and offering to god Svayambhudēva of Muḍiyanapalli situated in Nāgarakhaṇḍa-70 of Banavāsi-12000 division. Udayāditya is stated to have been governing the latter country and also Siṁtale-nāḍu from his capital at Baḷḷigāve.

cells.place: Slab inside the Mahādeva temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1131, Śukla, Āśvayuja śu. 13, Monday = 1209 A.D., September 13. The week day was Sunday.
cells.remarks: Records certain gifts made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Bijjarasa, son of ... of ... god ... and ... Rēvaṇēśvara, Kaṇṇēśvara, Kēdāra and Nāgēśvara called Gaṇa-maṭha. The gift was entrusted to Bilavvedēva and to another group of temples of Singēśvara, Bīrēśvara, Rēvaṇēśvara, Kaṇṇēśvara, Kēdāra and Nāgēśvara called Gaṇa-maṭha. The gift was entrusted to Bilavvedēva. It is stated that the gifts were made in the presence of Prabhu Nārāyaṇa ... and 1000 Mahājanas of ... the Pañcha-maṭha of Yiṅguḷige in Aralu-300. Lakshmīdēva-daṇḍanāyaka was governing as Mahāpradhāna at that time. Also records a gift of land etc. by Guṇḍabōva of Tonase to the Gaṇa-maṭha. The record was written by the Prabhu Nāgarasa.

cells.place: Slab fixed to the wall of the Jaina-dēguḷa
cells.date: Chālukya-Vikrama 18, Śrīmukha, Phālguṇa śu. 10, Monday=1094 A.D. February 27.
cells.remarks: Refers to Jākala-dēvī, queen of Tribhuvanamalla, as ruling over Iṅguḷige in Aruṇūru-300. It is stated that this queen built the Jaina temple at Iṅguḷige, installed an image of Pārśvanātha in it and entrusted it to Indrasēna-bhaṭṭāraka with certain grants necessary for its maintenance. A certain Aṇega is stated to have remitted some income to the same temple as sarvanamasya. The record was written by Nāgārjuna paṇḍita.

cells.place: Another slab in Kāliṅgēśvara temple †
cells.date: Chālukya - Vikrama 48, Siddhārthi, Māgha śu. 7, Saturday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Records the grant by Mahimaṇḍalēśvara Bibbarasa and Gonkarasa to the temple of god Bibbiśvara constructed by the former at Maritūru for the burning of a lamp in the temple of the same temple, a total of 6 mattars and 600 kammas of land. A further grant of 57 kammas of land is also recorded. The gift seems to have been made on occasion of a solar eclipse. A detailed account of the genealogies of Bibbarasa and Gonkarasa is given.

cells.location: Munirābād
cells.place: Slab in the temple of Śiva.
cells.date: Cālukya-Vikrama 13, expired, Īśvara, Vaiśākha su. 1, Monday, wrong for Vaiśākha su. 3, Akshayatritīyā, Monday, samkrānti = 1088 A.D., March 27, f.d.t. 30.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land by Sūndarārabhaṭṭa, the ūrodeya of Pulige (also called Vyāghra, grāma) and his wife Mañchikabbe and Sōmayya, granting land to the temple of Śiva and garden to the same deity made by the fiftytwo mahājanas of the place is also recorded. Specified shares in the income from grant-land were allotted to the worshipping Brāhmaṇa, the bhaṭṭa reciting the purāṇa in the presence of the god and four Brāhmaṇas feeding etc., besides enjoined that rice, ghee, betel-leaves and nuts etc. for the offering to the god should be provided from out of the same income. Similar provisions were made for the repairs of the temple and for a satra to feed twelve Brāhmaṇas. A supplementary grant made on a sun-stroke of the year Parābhava is referred to on this top portion of the stone. Published in Hyderabad Archaeological Series, No. 5.

RAJASTHAN
BHARATPUR DISTRICT
KAMAN TAHSIL
Kāman.—Chaurāsi Khamba temple.

cells.remarks: Damaged. cells.date: Vikrama 1236, Kār-tika śu. 1, Wed-nesday-1179 A.D., October 3.
cells.remarks: States that when the king's son Kumārasimha was in charge of Mändavyapura, and when Kirtipāla was his Rājyavā-haka Rājyasēvaka Vishayī Dhāravāraha of Guhila-gōtra made nyavasthā in the presence of the Sachchidēvī. The conditions of the bhōjakas should keep watch at the gate of the Sachchidēvī temple for one prahara and get one karsha, etc., every day from the kōsh-thāgāra of the temple. Published in Jaina Inscriptions Pt., I, p. 198. Cf. Bhandarkar's List, No. 384.

cells.place: Stone slab in three pieces kept in the compound of the Śāntinātha temple.
cells.date: (1) Vikrama 1283, Jyēshṭha śu. 8, Thursday = 1226 A.D., May 7, (the tithi was śu. 9).
cells.remarks: Contains two records. (1) Mentions Āśārāja of Naḍūla, his son Alhaṇa, his son Gaja-siṁha of Maṇḍōra, his son Mānasiṁha and also Yaśōdhara who was the minister of Udayasiṁha. Records that rājya Ābhaṭa, son of Āsaṭa who belonged to the prāgvāṭa community, made a gift of land to the deity Śāntinātha and established the Śāntinātha-pādukā-pīṭha in the village Valadaitha for the religious merit of Mānasiṁha. Also records that Rāja Ābhaṭa, along with his sons, made a gift of one dramma for the pūjā of the same deity.
